reader.requirement: At 1985 the ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause's data-name-1 may be written qualified by group, record and file-name qualifiers (§1985:IV.4.3.8.1 format 1), must then identify one item uniquely, and must lie in a record of the file (SR2).

edition-consulted.switches: Year == 2002 admits subscripted file-clause operands (FileControlBinder.Resolve ScreenClauseOperandOccurrence); false at 85 and 2023
the SOURCE phrase (record-key-name) is a 2002+ construct, refused at 85 with COBOL0900

reader.edition-search: grep DialectLevel|CobolVersion|Edition. in FileControlBinder.Resolve.cs: only SubscriptedClauseOperands and Edition.Cite (message text); the 85 sum-counter arm (kb/Work PB5361) applies only to a report sum counter
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness qualifies the alternate key in a passing program; not exercised are the file-name qualifier, an unqualified name declared twice, and a qualifier that reaches an item outside the file's records

probes.printed: ALT1 0002BRAVO rest2 FS=00 / ALT2 0003CHARLYrest3 FS=00 / PRI1 0003CHARLYrest3 FS=00 / START3 INVALID FS=23 / DONE
probes.expected: ALTERNATE RECORD KEY IS K-NAME IN K-AREA OF IX-REC (two levels) and K-NAME OF IGF (file-name qualifier) accepted; the alternate key orders START/READ NEXT

probes.printed: error COBOL1639: ALTERNATE RECORD KEY 'K-NAME' does not uniquely identify a data item — 2 declarations match
probes.expected: K-NAME declared in IX-REC and WS-K: must be qualified

probes.printed: error COBOL0863: ALTERNATE RECORD KEY 'K-NAME' references an item outside this file's record descriptions ... (ANSI §1985:IX.2.5.3 SR2)
probes.expected: K-NAME IN WS-K qualifies to a WS item: refused by SR2

probes.printed: error COBOL0900: the SOURCE phrase of the RECORD KEY or ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause requires COBOL-2002 (targeting COBOL-85)
probes.expected: a later edition's key form refused at 85

citations.check: OK  §1985:IX.2.5.3 SR1  (║2.5.3 Syntax Rules║)  the text is in SR1
OK  §1985:IV.4.3.8.1 SRL2.1  (4.3.8.1 Qualification)  the text is in SRL2.1

reader.notes: Both key clauses capture the IN/OF chain through ClauseDataNameSubscripted and resolve it with IdentifyDataName over the program scope, then SR2 judges the item; group, record and file-name qualifiers resolve, and an ambiguous or out-of-file operand is refused at --std 85.

refuter.evidence: At --std 85: 'ALTERNATE RECORD KEY IS AK OF AG OF REC2 IN IXF WITH DUPLICATES', with AK also in REC1 and in WS, the key in the FD's second record (E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/reread-1985-moved/out/refute-1985-m02/src/ks_ix.cob, runs/ks_ix-001: START KEY >= AK IN AG IN IXF 'YYY' then READ NEXT gives 0002YYYbbb, FS=00); a qualifier that names another file is refused by SR2 (E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/reread-1985-moved/out/refute-1985-m02/src/ks_ix_wrongfile.cob: COBOL0863 'ALTERNATE RECORD KEY AX references an item outside this file's record descriptions ... (ANSI §1985:IX.2.5.3 SR2)' for 'AX OF IX1' under IX2); a subscripted key, which the 1985 format (data-name-1, not identifier) does not admit, is refused (E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/reread-1985-moved/out/refute-1985-m02/src/ks_sub.cob: COBOL2024 'KA OF R1 (1)' is written with a subscript). cite.py: 'OK  §1985:IX.2.5.3 SR1', 'OK  §1985:IX.2.5.3 SR2'.
